meshelium.popup.opengl.title: Meshelium needs the Vulkan renderer
meshelium.popup.opengl.body: Meshelium is installed, but Minecraft is drawing with its OpenGL renderer, so Meshelium is staying off. Meshelium's faster terrain rendering only works on the Vulkan renderer. You can switch right here; the change takes effect the next time the game starts. You can also switch any time in Options > Video Settings > Graphics API.
meshelium.popup.restart.title: Restart Minecraft to apply
meshelium.popup.restart.body: Done: the Vulkan renderer is now selected. Minecraft only switches renderers while starting up, so the change applies the next time you launch the game.
meshelium.popup.no_mesh.title: Meshelium is staying off
meshelium.popup.no_mesh.body: The Vulkan renderer is running, but this computer's graphics card or driver doesn't offer the mesh shader feature Meshelium needs (VK_EXT_mesh_shader). Minecraft will keep rendering the normal way: everything works, just without Meshelium's speed-up. A newer graphics driver may add support on some cards.
meshelium.popup.vulkan_failed.title: Vulkan didn't start
meshelium.popup.vulkan_failed.body: The Vulkan renderer is selected in your settings, but Minecraft couldn't start it and fell back to the OpenGL renderer, so Meshelium is staying off. A graphics driver update may fix this. The renderer setting is in Options > Video Settings > Graphics API.
meshelium.options.title: Meshelium Options
meshelium.options.fog_end.label: Fog Ends At: %s%% of view (%s blocks)
meshelium.options.tooltip.fog: Minecraft's distance haze stops at a fixed 1024 blocks however far you can see, so past 64 chunks it covers most of the view. Off removes it and keeps the short fade at the very edge. Match View Distance moves it out with your render distance instead.
meshelium.options.tooltip.fog_end: How far out the haze finishes, as a share of how far you can see. 100%% ends it right at the horizon. Lower for a moodier, hazier look, higher for a clearer one.
meshelium.options.advanced.title: Meshelium Advanced
meshelium.options.advanced.locked: Meshelium is not running, so these settings will not do anything until it is. See the main Meshelium settings screen for why.
meshelium.options.plant_cull.label: Cull Tiny Plants Beyond: %s
meshelium.options.detail_cull.label: Cull Sub-Pixel Detail Beyond: %s
meshelium.options.smart_leaves.label: Smart Leaves Beyond: %s
meshelium.options.solid_leaves.label: Solid Leaves Beyond: %s
meshelium.options.max_rd.label: Distance Cap: %s
meshelium.options.occlusion_rd.label: Auto turns on at: %s chunks
meshelium.options.applies.world: Applies the next time a world loads.
meshelium.options.applies.rebuild: Applies now; chunks rebuild for a few seconds.
meshelium.options.applies.new_builds: Applies to terrain as it builds; the world catches up over a few seconds.
meshelium.options.applies.restart: Applies at the next game start.
meshelium.options.status.ready: Meshelium: READY, renders when a world opens
meshelium.options.status.reason.error: a renderer error occurred; vanilla is drawing
meshelium.chat.error.renderer: Meshelium hit a graphics error and handed the terrain back to Minecraft for the rest of this session. The game log has the details.
meshelium.chat.error.coverage: Meshelium could not fit all of this world's terrain on your graphics card, so Minecraft is drawing it instead. Rejoin the world to try again.
meshelium.chat.error.residency: Meshelium hit a problem preparing terrain and stopped drawing it. The game log has the details.
meshelium.chat.error.grow: Your graphics card refused the extra memory a longer render distance needs, so this world keeps the distance it started with.
meshelium.chat.seam.demoted: Meshelium is putting Minecraft's own terrain back. Chunks will rebuild for a few seconds.
meshelium.chat.seam.freeing: Meshelium is freeing Minecraft's duplicate copy of the terrain. Chunks will rebuild for a few seconds.
meshelium.chat.swap: Reloading the terrain so the renderers can swap. Chunks will rebuild for a few seconds.
meshelium.options.status.reason.passive: GPU budget exceeded; passive for this world
terrain memory %s MiB reached its %s MiB ceiling; passive for this world
one section's %s MiB mesh exceeded the %s MiB staging ring; passive for this world
region budget exhausted (%s of %s ids); passive for this world
your graphics card refused another %s MiB of terrain memory (%s MiB budget); passive for this world
a section failed to encode; passive for this world
meshelium.options.status.memory_free: Terrain memory: %s MB (%s MB free on the card)
meshelium.options.tooltip.status: Chunk sections are the 16 by 16 by 16 blocks Minecraft draws the world in. While Meshelium is running this counts the ones on screen, so it changes as you look around.
meshelium.options.tooltip.max_rd: How far Minecraft's own render distance slider is allowed to go. This does not change your distance by itself, it just raises the limit so you can pick a bigger number in Video Settings.
meshelium.options.tooltip.max_rd_custom: Type an exact limit, up to 120. That is as high as Minecraft can send a render distance. Big numbers use a lot of memory.
meshelium.options.tooltip.terrain: The whole mod, on or off. Meshelium draws terrain with mesh shaders, a faster way for the graphics card to handle lots of blocks. Off hands terrain back to Minecraft.
meshelium.options.tooltip.suppress_vanil: Minecraft keeps a second copy of the terrain in graphics memory even though Meshelium is the one drawing it. Freeing it saves several gigabytes at long render distances and costs nothing. Choose Kept only if another mod needs Minecraft's own terrain buffers. Changing this reloads the terrain, so chunks rebuild for a few seconds.
meshelium.options.tooltip.arena_trim: Meshelium grows its terrain memory in large steps and normally keeps the spare room committed. With this on, after half a minute of no terrain activity it hands the unused part back to your graphics card, which can be several hundred megabytes at long render distances. Flying somewhere new simply takes the memory again. Turn it off only if another mod misbehaves when graphics memory shrinks.
meshelium.options.tooltip.greedy_meshing: Merges neighbouring block faces into single larger ones, so there is less geometry to draw. How much it saves depends on Smooth Lighting: with it off it removes about one face in six, with it on nearer one in twenty, because Minecraft shades each corner separately and two differently shaded faces usually cannot become one. Expect a few percent more frames, most of it at long render distances. The picture is identical either way.
meshelium.options.tooltip.plant_cull: Past this distance, small plants like grass and flowers are not drawn. They are smaller than a pixel long before this matters, so the view should look the same and draw a little faster. Off draws everything, everywhere.
meshelium.options.tooltip.detail_cull: Past this distance, anything that would end up smaller than one pixel on your screen is skipped. Off draws everything.
meshelium.options.tooltip.smart_leaves: Past this distance, new terrain drops the leaf faces hidden inside tree canopies, which in a forest is roughly a fifth of all geometry. Leaves keep their see-through look: only faces buried where you could never see them are dropped. Trees regain their full detail as you approach, and turning this down or off rebuilds the affected chunks over a few seconds. Off changes nothing.
meshelium.options.tooltip.solid_leaves: Past this distance, see-through blocks like leaves are built fully solid, the way Fast graphics draws them everywhere. This helps most in big forests, and it lets distant woods hide whatever is behind them instead of drawing it. Trees regain their see-through look as you approach, and turning this down or off rebuilds the affected chunks over a few seconds. Off changes nothing.
meshelium.options.tooltip.debug_stats: Writes a line about the renderer to your log every 5 seconds. Handy in a bug report. Does not change how the game looks or runs.
meshelium.options.tooltip.popup: Show the startup notice again if Meshelium cannot run, for example when Minecraft is using the OpenGL renderer.
meshelium.options.tooltip.enable_vulkan: Selects the Vulkan renderer in Minecraft's own settings. The switch happens at the next game start.
meshelium.options.gate.opengl: Meshelium is off: Minecraft is drawing with OpenGL. Switch to Vulkan and these settings come alive at the next game start.
meshelium.options.gate.no_mesh: Meshelium is off: this graphics card or driver has no mesh shader support (VK_EXT_mesh_shader).
meshelium.options.gate.unknown: Meshelium is still checking the graphics backend. These settings unlock once it has.
meshelium.options.gate.vulkan_failed: Vulkan is selected but Minecraft couldn't start it and fell back to OpenGL, so Meshelium is off. A graphics driver update may fix this.
meshelium.options.dev_override: Some rows are locked: a -D dev flag on the command line is overriding them for this session.
meshelium.options.tooltip.occlusion: Skips drawing terrain that is hidden behind other terrain. It helps on some systems and hurts on others, and mostly only pays off at longer render distances. Auto switches it on past the distance where it usually helps. Safe to try either way.
meshelium.options.tooltip.occlusion_rd: The render distance Auto switches it on at. Lower it if you play mostly on the ground or in caves, raise it if you fly a lot. On laptop or integrated graphics, try 32.
meshelium.options.tooltip.occlusion_rd_c: Type an exact distance. 2 keeps it always on, 120 keeps it off.
meshelium.options.tooltip.reset: Puts every Meshelium setting back to normal. Minecraft's own settings are left alone.
meshelium.rd.clamped.title: Render distance limited to %s
meshelium.rd.clamped.off: Meshelium isn't drawing here, so the extended render distance was turned back down. The vanilla renderer above 32 chunks would run far too slowly.
meshelium.rd.clamped.passive: Meshelium went passive for this world (terrain didn't fit its GPU budget), so the render distance was restored for smooth play. It can be raised again in a fresh world.
meshelium.rd.restored.title: Render distance back to %s
meshelium.rd.restored.body: Meshelium is drawing again, so the distance it had to turn down while it was off has been put back.
meshelium.rd.rejoin.title: Rejoin to apply fully
meshelium.rd.rejoin.body: Render distance %s needs bigger GPU buffers than this world could grow to (sized %s chunks). Everything keeps working; rejoin the world to apply the full distance.
meshelium.rd.pressure.title: Render distance lowered to %s
meshelium.rd.pressure.body: Meshelium ran out of room on your graphics card for terrain this far out, so it pulled the distance in rather than let chunks go missing. It stays where it is now; raise it again in Video Settings whenever you like.
